thread.title: Intraday Update: A Tired Dow Slumps 100 Points

author: Crystal Kim
title: Intraday Update: A Tired Dow Slumps 100 Points
text:
By Crystal Kim July 30, 2018 1:26 p.m. ET Time Out. Markets appear fatigued and inconsolable. Earnings beats, coupled with optimistic management guidance and robust economic expansion couldn't move the Dow Jones Industrial Average . Virtually nothing is giving stocks enough juice to break out of its 2018 holding pattern of ups and downs. Apple (AAPL) earnings loom, but perhaps growth stocks are handing off the baton to value stocks. In today's Intraday Update, we...
Illustration: Bryan Thomas/Getty Images •...wonder what's eating the stock market;
•...entertain the end of growth stocks' run;
•...revel in the bright spots of the markets (financials); Affiliated Managers Group (AMG) is up nearly 5%.
What Have You Done For Me Lately? Market despondence in the middle of what has been a rather good earnings season is disconcerting, to say the least. The Dow Jones Industrial Average has fallen nearly 100 points or 0.4% to 25,353.31. Meanwhile the S&P 500 has slipped 0.5% to 2803.81 and the Nasdaq Composite has declined more than 1% to 7635.41.
Most companies have beaten earnings and sales expectations and although the surprises are beneath the long-term average, they are the highest in seven quarters, according to Bank of America Merrill Lynch 's Savita Subramanian . Management guidance also continues to be positive with "no cracks in the outlook," she says. In earnings calls, terms such as "better" or "stronger" compared to "worse" or "weaker" have been mentioned more frequently than they have on average in years past.
Sector-wise, energy stocks have seen greater rewards for beating consensus expectations, while consumer-discretionary stocks have seen greater punishment for missing expectations. Overall, reactions to earnings misses have been more brutal with stocks underperforming by 3.6 percentage points compared to the average of 2.4 percentage points.
If this earnings season sets the tone for the rest of the year and beyond, operating margins will take the spotlight from growth avenues as more executives focused on pricing power, supply chains and recurring pressure from labor, payroll, currency, oil as well as inflation and investments. "Sell-side operating-margin forecasts are tracking lower than early June levels for more than a third of the S&P 500 companies that had reported through Wednesday," according to Lori Calvasina , head of U.S. equity strategy at RBC Capital Markets . She also observed that overall reporting season has been better to favorites in large-cap value than large-cap growth.
Perhaps, a correction–the biggest since Feb. 5–is on its way, writes Michael Wilson , equity strategist at Morgan Stanley . Stocks were showing signs of " exhaustion " Friday as Amazon.com 's (AMZN) strong showing failed to inspire upward movement among the broad market indexes. Meanwhile the rotation to defensive sectors such as utilities and staples from cyclicals such as technology and discretionary, appears to be on its way.
"We have been out on a limb the past month with our defensive rotation call; and truth be told, we haven't had much interest from clients wanting to follow us down this path," writes Wilson. "Nevertheless, since our upgrade of Utilities on June 18th, defensive sectors have meaningfully outperformed." Not to mention Wilson's call to ease off on technology turned out to be a prescient: Tech leaders posted weaker earnings, and Netflix (NFLX) as well as Facebook (FB) fell flat on their faces.
Bottom line: "The selling has just begun," says Wilson.
Midday Movers Affiliated Managers Group (AMG) is up 4.8% to $158.30 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The money manager earned $3.61 a share on revenue of $600.1 million. Analysts were looking for earnings of $3.59 on revenue of $604.7 million.
Cooper (COO) is up 0.6% to $255.46 after Keybanc Capital Markets upgraded the medical-device company to Overweight, as the firm has "increased confidence in its current growth profile despite all the competitive noise, and it's trading at an attractive relative value historically to the peer group."
Diamond Offshore (DO) is up 5% to $20.05 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The energy firm lost 33 cents a share on revenue of $268.9 million. Analysts were looking for a loss of 39 cents a share on revenue of $279.8 million.
Oceaneering International (OII) is up 3.2% to $26.87 after Gabelli upgraded the offshore-energy-services provider to Buy, arguing that it has "unique set of assets in the oilfield service industry, continues to generate free cash flow and maintains a strong balance sheet."
Illustration: Ed Schipul Sohu.com (SOHU) is down 14.5% to $26.24 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The Chinese media firm lost $1.27 per American depositary share on revenue of $486.01 million. Analysts were looking for a loss of $1.50 per ADS on revenue of $506.79 million. For the full year, it sees a loss of $1.40 to $1.65 per ADS, on revenue of $445 million to $470 million. Consensus calls for a loss of 96 cents per ADS on revenue of $556.7 million. –Teresa Rivas
